Complete Empirical Research Plan  

============================================================

1. Identification Strategy  
——————————————————————  
• Primary design: Fuzzy regression-discontinuity design (FRD) at the 65th birthday.  
 – Running variable = exact age (in quarters in NHIS, in years in BRFSS, single-year in admin files).  
 – The probability of being insured rises sharply but not from 0→1, so age 65 is an instrument for (near-universal) Medicare coverage.  
• Extensions:  
 a. 2 × RD (difference-in-discontinuities) across race/ethnicity/education strata to measure disparity narrowing.  
 b. Event-study graphs (age profiles from 60–70) as visual validity and dynamic treatment-effect checks.

Why appropriate?  
– Assignment (turning 65) is predetermined and not manipulable.  
– Coverage jumps discretely at that cutoff.  
– Very rich micro-data with exact ages on both sides of the threshold allow local comparisons.

2. Treatment and Control  
————————————————  
Treatment variable (first stage)  
 Medicare coverage = 1 if respondent reports Part A or Part B coverage (or if hospital record lists Medicare as primary payer).

Instrument / running variable  
 Age – measured in decimal years or quarters.

Cutoff  
 c = 65.00 years (quarter = 260 when age in quarters).  
 We omit a small “donut” (e.g., ±0.25 yr) around the threshold to avoid birthday-month reporting noise.

Local treated group (LATE)  
 Individuals just above age 65 (“treated” by high probability of Medicare).

Local control group  
 Individuals just below age 65, within a chosen bandwidth (e.g., h = 2 years on either side), who have almost identical age trends but mostly are not yet on Medicare.

Timing  
 For hospital discharges and mortality, age is calculated at date of admission/death; therefore treatment is applied immediately at the 65th birthday.

3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
——————————————————  
A1. Continuity of potential outcomes in age: In the absence of Medicare, outcomes would evolve smoothly through age 65. Plausible—physiological aging is continuous; no other national health-policy shock happens exactly at 65.  
A2. No precise manipulation of the running variable: People cannot misreport their date of birth by enough to alter Medicare eligibility; hospital coders use administrative DOB. Very plausible.  
A3. First-stage relevance: Insurance probability jumps sharply (≈ +8 p.p. overall, +20 p.p. for minorities) at 65. Documentable in data.  
A4. Exclusion (for 2SLS interpretation): Other age-65 changes (retirement, Social Security) affect outcomes only through insurance within the chosen narrow bandwidth or can be controlled for. Plausible for short windows; we will probe by adding labor-force status controls and by using even narrower bandwidths.  
A5. Stable unit treatment value (SUTVA): One person’s Medicare eligibility does not change another’s outcome in this narrow age neighborhood. Reasonable.

4. Main Threats and Mitigation  
—————————————————  
T1. Concurrent retirement/Social-Security claiming may independently alter utilization.  
 • Mitigation:  
  – Estimate within ≤1 year bandwidths where retirement rates do not jump as sharply as coverage.  
  – Control for labor-force status (NHIS & BRFSS) or use subgroup of already-retired workers.  
  – Show placebo RD at 62 (early Social-Security) and 66/67 (full retirement age in later cohorts).  
T2. Discrete changes in sample composition (e.g., survey sampling frames change at 65).  
 • Mitigation: Test RD in predetermined covariates (race, education, state, pre-existing chronic conditions) to confirm smoothness.  
T3. Age-heaping / coarse age measurement (BRFSS age in years).  
 • Mitigation:  
  – Prefer NHIS (age in quarters) for main estimates.  
  – In BRFSS implement “fuzzy bin RD” à la Kolesár & Rothe (2018) or group RD by age-in-years cells.  
  – Donut RD excluding exactly “age 65” in whole-year files.

5. R Code Outline (simplified)  
—————————————————
```r
# Packages
library(data.table)
library(fixest)        # fast OLS/IV
library(rdrobust)      # RD estimation
library(sandwich)      # robust vcov for fixest
library(modelsummary)

# 1. Load NHIS sample (assumed CSV)
nhis <- fread("nhis_92_01.csv")

# 2. Construct variables ----------------------------------
nhis[, age_yrs  := age_quarter/4]            # convert quarters → years
nhis[, treat65  := (age_yrs >= 65)]          # indicator for being 65+
nhis[, age_c    := age_yrs - 65]             # centered running var
nhis[, insured  := medicare_cov == 1]        # binary coverage
nhis[, outcome  := doctor_visits]            # example outcome

# 3. Bandwidth (2 years each side)
bw <- 2
sample <- nhis[age_c >= -bw & age_c <= bw & age_c != 0]

# 4a. First-stage: jump in coverage
fs <- rdrobust(y = sample$insured, x = sample$age_c, c = 0,
               p = 1, h = bw)
summary(fs)

# 4b. Reduced-form: jump in utilization
rf <- rdrobust(y = sample$outcome, x = sample$age_c, c = 0,
               p = 1, h = bw)
summary(rf)

# 4c. 2SLS FRD with local linear weights -------------------
# Generate triangular kernel weights
sample[, w := ifelse(age_c>=0, 1 - abs(age_c)/bw, 1 - abs(age_c)/bw)]
ivreg <- feols(outcome ~ insured | treat65, data = sample, weights = ~w,
               vcov = "hetero")
etable(ivreg)

# 5. Robustness: placebo cutoff at 62
sample62 <- nhis[abs(age_yrs - 62) <= bw]
sample62[, age_c62 := age_yrs - 62]
placebo <- rdrobust(y = sample62$outcome, x = sample62$age_c62, c = 0,
                    p = 1, h = bw)
summary(placebo)
```
(Analogous code would be repeated for hospital-discharge and mortality data; for count outcomes we would use `fepois` in `fixest`.)

6. Expected Results  
—————————————  
Direction: Obtaining Medicare should increase access and utilization: more doctor visits, hospital admissions for elective procedures, preventive screenings; it may reduce delayed/forgone care.  
Magnitude: Prior literature suggests ~15–25 percent increase in physician visits and elective hospitalizations; ~8 p.p. drop in uninsured; ~5–10 p.p. increase in receipt of flu shots, cholesterol checks; limited immediate changes in self-reported health; small but non-zero reductions in 70+ mortality within 5-10 years. Disparity gaps (black-white, low-high education) in coverage and access should shrink by roughly 60–75 percent at the cutoff.

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (for RD)  
————————————————————————  
C1 – Smoothness of baseline covariates: 1 (will verify; likely satisfied)  
C2 – No manipulation of running variable: 1  
C3 – Strong first stage: 1  
C4 – No other policy discontinuity at cutoff: 0.5 (retirement confounder; partly addressed)  
C5 – Robustness to bandwidth, polynomial order, placebo tests: 1  

Total score = 4.5 / 5  

============================================================
This plan uses the age-65 Medicare eligibility threshold as a powerful quasi-experiment to estimate the causal impact of universal insurance on health care use, behaviors, and outcomes, while explicitly testing and addressing the key threats to identification.
